Be sure to call the base class `VisualInstance::_physics_interpolated_changed()` here as it isn't done for you.
(I don't know whether this is already done in 4.x for the 3D, but it is in 3.x).

~~I think the correct one would be `CanvasItem::_physics_interpolated_changed();`. I actually had that in an earlier draft but that required me to make the `protected` (currently `private`). I'll look into it and see if I might've missed something with Node2D~~

Edit:
```
[ 81%] scene/2d/multimesh_instance_2d.cpp: In member function 'virtual void MultiMeshInstance2D::_physics_interpolated_changed()':
scene/2d/multimesh_instance_2d.cpp:53:46: error: 'virtual void CanvasItem::_physics_interpolated_changed()' is private within this context
   53 |         Node2D::_physics_interpolated_changed();
      |         ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~
In file included from ./scene/2d/node_2d.h:33,
                 from scene/2d/multimesh_instance_2d.h:33,
                 from scene/2d/multimesh_instance_2d.cpp:31:
./scene/main/canvas_item.h:143:22: note: declared private here
  143 |         virtual void _physics_interpolated_changed() override;
      |                      ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

```

So ~~CanvasItem~~ Node2D seems to be correct? But it's `_physics_interpolated_changed()` is probably private for a reason?
Oh yeah good point let me look.

In this case the parent class is `Node2D` but it should call down to `Node` and it's protected so can be called.

It's just a stub so should be compiled out, but works if we add in later functionality. I likely forgot to call it on some of the other 2D nodes, but sensible to put in if it compiles.

`Node2D::_physics_interpolated_changed()`

_(I'll likely check this if adding something in a parent class, but no harm putting it in now.)_

Using `Node` does compile and work but I had a thought (feel free to dismiss it if it's unrelated or not important):   

> The MultiMesh interpolation state _can_ be different from the Node (MultiMeshInstance2D) interpolation state (on/off/inherit). While testing I came across the, probably unusual combination of having the MultiMesh be NOT interpolated but moving the MultiMeshInstance2D note with interpolation. This resulted in smoothed movement when moving the node but unsmoothed movement when setting an instance transform on the multimesh itself.

Not sure if that is something to consider (probably not). 

**Anyways...**
As stated: Using `Node` works but if I see it correctly, the inheritance chain is something like this:
`Node -> CanvasItem -> Node2D -> ... -> MultiMeshInstance2D`

While `Node` has no real implementation for `_physics_interpolated_changed()`, `CanvasItem` does. So calling the `Node` implementation directly would omit the `CanvasItem` code. (`CanvasItem` `_physics_interpolated_changed()` is also private). I am not deep enough into the codebase to know if this could lead to any issues down the line (probably not as basically all other nodes work fine with regards to toggling physics interpolation). 

Other than that, it seems to be working. If the above seems fine I'll commit the change

Oh I see, I forgot `Node2D` is derived from `CanvasItem`, in that case, yeah just make the canvas item version protected, that's fine .. I likely either put it in the wrong category, or figured I'd change it when required.

This may actually be the first 2D node that requires this (hence the extra step).

I'm not actually sure whether `MultiMeshInstance2D` actually _uses_ the canvas item RID, but it seems safer.
Alright. Will push another commit with the changes :)
